plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with consequential-damages exclusion, defined Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnity, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, IP) and anti-failure-of-remedy language. Check cap size against contract value and confirm Excluded Claims sit outside the cap, not just outside 21.2.

No Section 20 appears in the outline even though sec-9.3 cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' and sec-21.3 assumes 'indemnification obligations' exist. Treat as a missing Vendor indemnity (third-party IP, data/security, bodily injury/property damage, law violations) plus absent narrow Customer indemnity; verify the numbering gap is not merely an extraction omission before concluding.

sec-12.4-2 bars Customer from developing, marketing, selling or acquiring any competing product or service for the term plus 24 months in any territory — squarely walk-away territory. Note the direct conflict with sec-12.3, which states Customer has made no non-compete commitment; deletion of sec-12.4-2 is the clean fix.

sec-7.2 (first of two provisions numbered 7.2) conditions engaging another provider on disclosing and matching offers — a de facto right of first refusal limiting supplier freedom. sec-12.3 preserves our freedom to engage any supplier and disclaims exclusivity; flag the inconsistency. Avoid double-flagging the same match obligation under MFN unless both rules are independently breached.

Direction is wrong in sec-7.2: the disclose-and-match obligation runs against Customer (MFN/best-terms burden on us), contradicting sec-12.3's statement that no most-favoured-customer commitment was made. Coordinate with the EXCLUSIVITY plan so the same sentence is addressed once.

sec-12.4 bars soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for the term plus 24 months 'regardless of how the employee applies' — one-sided, unbounded as to employee population, and with no general-advertising or unsolicited-applicant carve-out. sec-12.3 (hiring anyone responding to general recruitment) is the counterweight to cite.

No convenience-termination right for Customer anywhere; sec-9 offers only cause-based rights (breach, insolvency, security/SLA/IP failures) and sec-2.1 expressly negates reduction or termination rights. Confirm the Vendor also lacks a convenience exit (it appears to), then treat as missing and anchor a Customer-only right near sec-9.1/9.5.

sec-8.2 gives a 30-day Customer non-renewal window plus a 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if the reminder is missed; sec-8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no uplift on prepaid periods. Likely compliant — confirm the uplift cap and notice mechanics rather than redlining.

sec-28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list — while sec-28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts. Flag the Singapore choice and the internal contradiction; New York law/venue is the natural landing spot. sec-28.3 (executive escalation) is acceptable pre-suit process.

sec-24.1 permits Customer affiliate/successor assignment without consent, sec-24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and delegation, and sec-24.4 denies Vendor any termination/repricing right on our change of control; sec-13.3 allows licence transfer to an affiliate or successor. Reads compliant — verify sec-24.3's residual consent requirement does not swallow sec-24.1.

sec-14.1 correctly keeps Customer Data and Customer IP with us, but sec-14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — a direction failure on work we pay for. Read against sec-1.4, sec-14.3 and the sec-13.2 perpetual licence when framing ownership versus paid-up-licence fallback.

sec-13.1 extends access to Affiliates and contractors and sec-13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, paid-up licence to delivered Vendor Technology, with sec-13.3 limiting revocation/suspension to uncured material breach after cure opportunity. The gap is sec-14.2's revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence — coordinate with the IP plan so the ownership point is not flagged twice.

sec-22.1 limits audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor; sec-22.2 puts costs on Vendor absent a >5% underpayment and bars access to our systems, unrelated Customer Data and privileged material; sec-22.3 makes findings our Confidential Information. Expect compliant.

No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination-fee payable by Customer appears; sec-7.3 bars interest on amounts found not due and sec-22.2 shortfall costs are compensatory. The take-or-pay in sec-2.1 is the nearest economic penalty but belongs under MINCOMMIT — do not double-flag. Also note no service-credit/SLA regime is visible in the outline.

sec-19.1–19.3 give professional-services, conformity, no-malicious-code and compliance warranties; sec-19.2 runs 90 days for Deliverables and the full subscription term for hosted Services; sec-19.4 provides re-performance then termination and refund, expressly non-exclusive for IP/security/indemnified claims; sec-19.5 preserves express warranties. Likely compliant.

sec-18.1 carries CGL 1M/2M, workers' comp, employer's liability 1M, E&O 2M and cyber/privacy 5M for the term plus one year; sec-18.2 adds certificates, primary coverage, cancellation notice and a no-limitation-of-liability statement. Check the E&O/cyber limits against data sensitivity, but the clause exists and is substantively adequate.

sec-2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay for three years expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — walk-away as drafted and directly contradicted by sec-12.3's no-minimum-volume disclaimer. Interacts with the absent T4C right; frame the commitment as needing an exit, carry-forward or reduction mechanism.

sec-10.1 assumes 'any agreed transition period' and sec-10.2 covers Deliverable delivery and refunds, but no clause obliges Vendor to provide priced transition assistance or to return/export Customer Data in a usable format on exit; sec-16.5 covers only Confidential Information return and cross-refers to a Section 11 that is absent from the outline. Treat as a partial clause with a material gap.
